newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot says plans to buy 10 Boeing 737s.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot says plans to buy 10 Boeing 737s.

text.p: Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines plans to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 passenger jets in 1997-98, paying for them over an extended period, Deputy Chief Executive Valery Okulov said Tuesday.
"We plan to operate these jets on routes of up to 3,000 km (1,880 miles) from Russia to Europe and we plan to develop our route network in Russia and the CIS as well," Okulov said.
He said a letter of intent was signed Sept. 3 at the Farnborough international air show in Britain.
"We want to replace our Tupolev 134s," said Okulov, referring to a short- or medium-haul Russian-made jet.

He declined to give details of the cost of the deal, involving new planes direct from the Boeing plant, or of the extended payments scheme. However, he noted that the average price for a 737-400 was $25 million to $30 million.
State-owned Aeroflot inherited its international routes from the former Soviet monopoly carrier, which broke up when the Soviet Union collapsed.

Aeroflot flies to 126 international destinations in 102 countries, including former Soviet republics. They have recently begun flying eight routes in Russia. Boeing's stock traded Tuesday at $90 a share, down 12.5 cents, on the New York Stock Exchange.
